q1_issues.issue: Both arguments are bare kind-denoting plurals, which the relational-generic rule routes to an opaque kind-level relation; the emitted per-instance all-pairs rule is exactly the 'distributing it to all instance-pairs' the instruction set warns against, asserting that every cold wind extinguishes every unprepared lantern anywhere.

q2_gaps: a relational generic whose kind NPs carry non-fusing descriptive modifiers ('cold winds', 'unprepared lanterns') - the both-arguments-bare-kind trigger fires, but the compound rules forbid fusing an incidental descriptive adjective into a kind symbol, so there is no licensed single kind term to put in the relation's two argument slots
notes: Splitting 'cold' and 'unprepared' off as separate Member properties on the instance variables is correct (incidental description, not a fusing classifier), 'unprepared' is rightly a positive property rather than a negation, and Agent on the inanimate transitive subject follows the rule.
